architecture.mechanism: Impact loading combined with high surface traction and contact pressure initiates micro-cracks and white etching areas (WEAs) at non-metallic inclusions, which propagate into white etching crack (WEC) networks that weaken the bearing subsurface and cause rolling contact fatigue flaking.
architecture.intervention: Modify the gear-mesh tooth surface finish (e.g., controlled superfinishing or micro-dimpling) to lower surface traction while retaining EHL film support, and add a high-viscosity-index PAO synthetic lubricant with a MoDTC/ZDDP additive package and an oil-journal back-flow restrictor to maintain a thicker, more robust elastohydrodynamic film at the rolling-sliding contact under variable load spikes.
architecture.expected_effect: Reduced Hertzian and shear stress concentration at inclusions during load transients, decreased subsurface micro-crack and WEA/WEC nucleation, and a more stable lubricating film that prevents mixed/boundary contact during low-speed/high-torque events, thereby extending bearing service life under variable loading.
architecture.falsification_test: Run twin-disc rolling contact fatigue tests on standard reference bearings versus surface-modified + enhanced-lubricant bearings, applying step-load profiles that simulate wind turbine torque transients; statistically compare (e.g., Weibull L10) the cycles to first inclusion-initiated micro-crack and WEA formation using sectioned, etched metallographic analysis, with the intervention validated only if it significantly increases cycles-to-initiation at p < 0.05.
